categories.main_business_segments: GDS Holdings Limited primarily develops and operates high-performance data centers in mainland China, offering colocation and managed services including managed hosting and managed cloud services. Additionally, it holds a significant minority equity investment (35.6%) in DayOne, which develops and operates data centers in Southeast Asia and Northeast Asia. The company’s data centers serve hyperscale cloud providers, large internet companies, financial institutions, telecommunications carriers, and large enterprises.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company employs advanced data center design with high power density (approximately 2.2 kW/sqm), high power efficiency (average PUE around 1.24 for newer centers), and multiple redundancy systems (2N or distributed N+1). It uses a modular construction approach with pre-fabrication technology to shorten development time and improve quality. GDS has developed proprietary data center operation management platforms and operational enhancement tools including AI and robotics to optimize performance and service delivery.
categories.primary_customers_markets: GDS serves hyperscale cloud service providers, large internet companies, financial institutions, telecommunications carriers, and large domestic and multinational corporations. Its customers include the largest PRC and global public cloud platforms. The company’s top two customers accounted for 33.7% and 14.3% of total area committed as of December 31, 2024. The customer agreements typically range from 1 to 10 years depending on customer type.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company operates predominantly in mainland China with data centers strategically located in Tier 1 markets including Shanghai, Beijing, Shenzhen, Guangzhou, Chengdu, and Chongqing. It also has a significant equity investment in DayOne, which operates data centers in Southeast Asia (Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia), Northeast Asia (Tokyo, Greater Bangkok), and Hong Kong. The company’s corporate structure includes subsidiaries and VIEs in mainland China, Hong Kong, Cayman Islands, Singapore, and other jurisdictions.
categories.supply_chain_position: GDS operates primarily as a developer and operator of data centers, positioned midstream in the data center services supply chain. It owns or leases data center facilities, provides colocation and managed services to end customers, and hosts major cloud platforms. The company also manages construction, design, and operations internally, and outsources certain on-site services. It acts as a service provider rather than a manufacturer or upstream infrastructure supplier.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: The company focuses on innovation in data center design and operations, emphasizing high power density, efficiency, and modular construction methods. It invests in proprietary operational platforms, AI, robotics, and smart building technologies to enhance service quality and efficiency. GDS also pursues strategic partnerships and acquisitions to expand capacity and geographic reach. Environmental sustainability and energy efficiency are key priorities, with initiatives to increase renewable energy use and reduce carbon emissions.
categories.revenue_model: GDS generates revenue primarily through recurring service fees from colocation and managed services, including managed hosting and managed cloud services. Pricing structures include variable consideration based on actual usage (especially power consumption) and fixed consideration contracts. The company also earns revenue from IT equipment sales and consulting services. Billing is typically monthly or quarterly in arrears, and revenue is recognized as services are rendered.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: GDS competes mainly with domestic and international carrier-neutral data center providers in China. It differentiates itself through its large-scale, high-performance data centers, extensive presence in Tier 1 markets, long operational track record, and strong relationships with telecommunications carriers and cloud providers. It also competes with state-owned telecommunications carriers but offers carrier-neutral connectivity to multiple networks. GDS is positioned as a leading data center service provider in China with a growing international presence through DayOne.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: As of December 31, 2024, GDS operated 91 self-developed data centers with 613,583 sqm net floor area in service and 102,691 sqm under construction. Net revenue grew by 5.5% annually from RMB9.3 billion in 2022 to RMB10.3 billion (US$1.41 billion) in 2024. Adjusted EBITDA increased to RMB4.88 billion (US$668 million) in 2024. The company reported net income of RMB3.3 billion (US$453 million) in 2024, including a gain on deconsolidation of DayOne. It maintains significant debt financing with total borrowings exceeding RMB29 billion as of 2024. The company’s equity investment in DayOne is a material contributor to overall results.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: GDS emphasizes its high-performance data centers characterized by large net floor area, high power density, high power efficiency, and multiple redundancy systems, enabling customers to deploy mission-critical IT infrastructure efficiently and reliably. Its carrier and cloud neutrality allows customers access to all major telecom networks and leading public clouds. The company’s proprietary operational platforms and innovative modular construction methods provide flexibility, scalability, and cost efficiency. GDS’s strategic locations in Tier 1 economic hubs and strong customer relationships with hyperscale cloud providers and large enterprises further differentiate its offerings.
